A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SwiLTra-Bench. Their text, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison; changed pagination does not indicate missing material.

before.justification: V1 reports original translation experiments, fine-tuning comparisons, human expert ratings, and judge-correlation results, including Tables C.1 and E.1.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and additionally evaluates an ensemble judge in Figure 6 and Table E.1.

M1.justification: Section 6.1, RQ4 adds SwiLTra-Judge-Ensemble, averaging four existing configurations: GPT-4o-mini and Gemini-1.5-Flash, each using codebook grading with single and diverse few-shot examples. The original judge is retained as SwiLTra-Judge-Single. This is a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same law, headnote, and press-release datasets and language coverage. Table 1 is unchanged. The expanded Romansh discussion describes existing coverage and its constraints, without establishing additional training or evaluation data.

E2.justification: The judge comparison in RQ4, Figure 6, and Table E.1 adds the ensemble as an evaluated alternative to the retained single judge. External metric comparators and translation-model comparison sets remain unchanged; more explicit Claude names identify existing models.

E3.justification: Existing splits, model sizes, training budgets, evaluation measures, and human-score filtering are retained. The ensemble uses the existing correlation and cross-validation evaluation. Changing 'at least two' annotators to 'exactly two' clarifies v1's already-stated averaging of two scores, without establishing a changed study design.

E4.justification: RQ4 adds an internal comparison testing whether averaging judge configurations improves alignment with human ratings over the best single configuration. Existing model, prompt, few-shot, scaling, and judge-harshness analyses remain; expanded explanations of annotator disagreement do not add a new analysis.

E5.justification: New Section 4.1 distinguishes descriptive comparisons from statistical significance claims. RQ3 removes its significance claim and p-value; RQ4 specifies unpaired t-tests with N = 368 per group. Bootstrap standard errors, 95% confidence intervals, and cross-validation reporting already existed; no increased run or seed count is documented.

E6.justification: Table E.1 adds ensemble Spearman correlation of 0.533 ± 0.080, versus the retained single judge's 0.504 ± 0.074. Existing bootstrap estimates and intervals change, including the single judge's 0.504 to 0.506. RQ4 changes the single-judge/XCOMET p-value from 0.0014 to 0.0008 and adds an ensemble comparison. Tables 1–5 and C.1 retain their values.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theoretical propositions or proofs. V2 adds an operational averaging procedure and statistical-test documentation, without introducing or revising a formal derivation or theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions and claims: the multilingual benchmark, broad model comparison, benefits and limits of fine-tuning, and a judge aligned with human assessments. The ensemble extends the supporting work without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 expands the Romansh coverage limitation and argues that alternative sources would compromise quality or alignment. Section 5.1 adds interpretive nuance and legal structure as explanations for agreement differences, while discounting calibration as the main cause. Section 4.1 also qualifies ordinary performance comparisons as descriptive.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly supplies the fine-tuning instruction template and explicitly states use of the entire training set. V2 also documents ensemble composition and averaging, clarifies annotator counts, and adds a separate GitHub code link alongside the retained dataset link. These disclosures do not establish retraining or changed hyperparameters.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited research remain the same. Shortened author lists for the Phi-3, Llama 3, and Gemma 2 references are bibliographic formatting changes, not additions or removals of prior work.

P1.justification: V2 adds a statistical-significance subsection, expands several explanatory passages, clarifies model terminology, and updates contact information and acknowledgments. Reference author lists are shortened. The main narrative and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 6 gains an ensemble bar, distinguishes Single from Ensemble, and rotates category labels. Table E.1 gains a row and reorders some entries. Author affiliations use logos, and several figures move with text reflow. All other existing result plots retain identical content.

improvement.justification: The explicit training prompt, separate code link, and clearer distinction between descriptive and significant findings modestly improve reproducibility and interpretation. The ensemble adds useful comparative evidence, although Table E.1 shows worse RMSE and MAE than the single judge, and unpaired tests on shared human-rated examples remain insufficiently justified. The core benchmark and translation evidence are unchanged.
